old: A verbless list of qualities closed by iti and the label amātya-sampat (glossary: sampat = excellence of X; label 'Such is X', iti = closing particle). jānapada = a person of the country (glossary: country people); the first quality is not 'native' in a stronger sense. svavagraha: printed as one word; sandhi su+a gives sva, so read su-avagrahaḥ 'of good restraint' (avagraha = restraint, as in unit 3); the alternative sva-avagraha would be written svāv-, so it is not adopted; sense of the whole (self-restraint, or 'easily restrained') is uncertain. kṛta-śilpa: literally 'one by whom skill is made'; read 'with skill acquired'. cakṣuṣmān: literally 'having eyes'; unit 3 shows the fuller 'treatise-eye' (śāstra-cakṣuṣmattā), not imported here. dhārayiṣṇu: literally 'holding'; 'retentive' follows dhārayiṣṇutā of unit 3. pratipattimān: pratipatti is left as 'grasp' (alternatives: understanding, presence of mind). stambha = stiffness (alternative: obstinacy, pride); cāpala = fickleness. sampriya: 'sam' read as 'thoroughly'. vairāṇām akartā: literally 'a non-maker of enmities'.
